Page and region selection are never treated as successive evidence decisions in a unified process.

Both policies are optimized with stage-wise GRPO using granularity-specific structured-set rewards. The answer model receives selected full pages plus region crops and OCR/table text to preserve global context while emphasizing fine-grained evidence.

Controlled ablations show selected regional evidence improves the page-only system in accuracy and F1 by 5.51% and 4.82%, respectively.
AI.conclusion: The results demonstrate that organizing coarse page routing and fine-grained region routing as successive, separately optimized stages of a unified evidence-acquisition process improves long-document visual question answering performance.

title: Scaling Properties of Text Conditioning in Visual Generation
comment: Code: https://github.com/heheyas/context-scaling Models: https://huggingface.co/collections/heheyas/context-scaling Demo: https://heheyas-context-scaling.hf.space/ Project page: https://heheyas.github.io/context-scaling
summary: We study empirical scaling properties for text conditioning in visual generation. Such properties have rarely been measured because diffusion loss does not scale with the number of tokens in natural-language prompts. Surprisingly, we find that the converged diffusion loss scales with the amount of structured language in the prompt. To quantify structured language, we adapt two complementary measures: a white-box likelihood metric (GPG) and a black-box attribute metric (ED). Across controlled training runs, the converged diffusion loss decreases approximately linearly with GPG and follows a power law with ED. Guided by these scaling properties, we improve \emph{diffusability} by constructing structured prompts with semantic and geometric annotations derived from images, and improve \emph{promptability} by training a prompter through supervised fine-tuning, cold-start, and verifier-gated on-policy distillation. The resulting system outperforms all evaluated open-weight models on nearly every compositional, reasoning, and world-knowledge benchmark, while matching or surpassing the strongest closed-weight models on most evaluations.

AI.tldr: This paper studies empirical scaling laws between text conditioning and visual generation quality, finding that diffusion loss scales with the amount of structured language in prompts. Using two complementary measures (GPG and ED), they show loss decreases linearly with GPG and follows a power law with ED. This motivates improving "diffusability" via structured prompts with semantic/geometric annotations and "promptability" via a trained prompter, achieving state-of-the-art results on compositional, reasoning, and world-knowledge benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Scaling properties for text conditioning in visual generation have rarely been measured because diffusion loss does not obviously scale with token count in natural-language prompts. Understanding these scaling properties could guide improvements to text-to-image generation.
AI.method: The authors (1) quantify structured language using two complementary measures: GPG (a white-box likelihood metric) and ED (a black-box attribute metric); (2) measure scaling behavior of converged diffusion loss across controlled training runs; (3) improve diffusability by constructing structured prompts with semantic and geometric annotations from images; (4) improve promptability by training a prompter via supervised fine-tuning, cold-start, and verifier-gated on-policy distillation.
AI.result: Converged diffusion loss decreases approximately linearly with GPG and follows a power law with ED. The resulting system outperforms all evaluated open-weight models on nearly every compositional, reasoning, and world-knowledge benchmark, and matches or surpasses the strongest closed-weight models on most evaluations.
AI.conclusion: Empirical scaling laws exist between structured language in prompts and diffusion loss, which can be exploited to improve both prompt construction (diffusability) and prompt generation (promptability), yielding state-of-the-art text-conditioned visual generation.

title: Toward Robust and 3D-Aware RGB-NIR Imaging in the Dark
comment: ACM Multimedia 2026, Codes and Models: https://github.com/MyNiuuu/3DarkFusion
summary: Robust low-light imaging remains challenging for the community. Recent studies have explored fusing Near-Infrared (NIR) with noisy RGB to achieve improved enhancement, yet most methods depend on carefully curated training data pairs, with limited robustness under different scenarios. This paper offers a new perspective for RGB-NIR low-light imaging by incorporating 3D-aware neural modeling. Without using clean RGB supervision, a powerful model can be optimized to implicitly fuse extremely noisy RGB observations with NIR cues in 3D space, effectively recovering clean RGB images. The proposed model obviates the requirement for clean RGB data collection, generalizes across different noise levels. Extensive evaluations on synthetic and real data demonstrate its superiority. Codes available: https://github.com/MyNiuuu/3DarkFusion

AI.tldr: Introduces a 3D-aware neural modeling approach for RGB-NIR low-light image fusion that removes the need for clean RGB supervision, enabling robust recovery of clean RGB images from extremely noisy observations with generalization across noise levels.
AI.motivation: Existing RGB-NIR low-light enhancement methods rely on carefully curated training pairs and lack robustness across different scenarios, limiting their practical applicability.
AI.method: Incorporates 3D-aware neural modeling to implicitly fuse extremely noisy RGB observations with NIR cues in 3D space, optimizing a powerful model without clean RGB supervision.
AI.result: Demonstrates superiority over existing methods on both synthetic and real data, with generalization across different noise levels.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework eliminates the dependency on clean RGB data collection while achieving robust low-light image recovery across varied scenarios.
